newsitem.title: ST LUCIA: Strike hits St. Lucia's banana farms.
newsitem.headline: Strike hits St. Lucia's banana farms.

text.p: A strike by farmers hit the first day of banana harvesting in the south of St. Lucia on Tuesday, police said.
Little cutting took place and groups of farmers gathered in groups along roads, they said. No unrest was reported.

Members of the farmers' Banana Salvation Committee voted on Sunday to go on strike in a dispute with the government over pricing and levies on cartons and what they say is their lack of involvement in banana industry policy.

Prime Minister Vaughan Lewis called the strike unjustified and said certain political interests were egging on farmers to enagage in violent acts. The government had made strenuous efforts to resolve the dispute, he said.
He also said that although farmers had the right to strike, police would crack down on anyone who tried to prevent others from working.
Bananas are a major source of foreign exchange for St. Lucia, one of the Windward Islands.
Three years ago two farmers were shot dead during a clash with police at the height of a strike during which property was vandalised.
